Since v0.23.21, the Tabularium has changed the default behaviour and database structure. The following changes have been made:

1. **Case sensitivity of filenames**
   The handling of filenames is now case-insensitive. This is a beneficial change for most platforms, other than Linux and iOS, which do not manage filename case sensitivity effectively.
   (On These, a warning will be displayed for files with the same name but different cases).

2. **Revision handling of the chunks**
   Chunks are immutable, which allows their revisions to be fixed. This change will enhance the performance of file saving.

___However, to enable either of these changes, both remote and local databases need to be rebuilt. This process takes a few minutes, and we recommend doing it when you have ample time.___

RedFlag.Fetch.Method.Desc:
How do you want to fetch?
- %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSafer}.
  **Low Traffic**, **High CPU**, **Low Risk**
  Recommended if ...
  - Files possibly inconsistent
  - Files were not so much
- %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSmoother}.
  **Low Traffic**, **Moderate CPU**, **Low to Moderate Risk**
  Recommended if ...
  - Files probably consistent
  - You have a lot of files.
- %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchTraditional}.
  **High Traffic**, **Low CPU**, **Low to Moderate Risk**

>[!INFO]- Details
> ## %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSafer}.
> **Low Traffic**, **High CPU**, **Low Risk**
> This option first creates a local database using existing local files before fetching data from the remote source.
> If matching files exist both locally and remotely, only the differences between them will be transferred.
> However, files present in both locations will initially be handled as conflicted files. They will be resolved automatically if they are not actually conflicted, but this process may take time.
> This is generally the safest method, minimizing data loss risk.
> ## %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSmoother}.
> **Low Traffic**, **Moderate CPU**, **Low to Moderate Risk** (depending operation)
> This option first creates chunks from local files for the database, then fetches data. Consequently, only chunks missing locally are transferred. However, all metadata is taken from the remote source.
> Local files are then compared against this metadata at launch. The content considered newer will overwrite the older one (by modified time). This outcome is then synchronised back to the remote database.
> This is generally safe if local files are genuinely the latest timestamp. However, it can cause problems if a file has a newer timestamp but older content (like the initial `welcome.md`).
> This uses less CPU and faster than "%{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSafer}", but it may lead to data loss if not used carefully.
> ## %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchTraditional}.
> **High Traffic**, **Low CPU**, **Low to Moderate Risk** (depending operation)
> All things will be fetched from the remote.
> Similar to the %{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSmoother}, but all chunks are fetched from the remote source.
> This is the most traditional way to fetch, typically consuming the most network traffic and time. It also carries a similar risk of overwriting remote files to the '%{RedFlag.Fetch.Method.FetchSmoother}' option.
> However, it is often considered the most stable method because it is the longest-established and most straightforward approach.

tabularium.help.connect.body:
Open Connection and sign in with your account on the Tabularium server. Choose an existing vault or create a new one, name this device, and enter the vault's passphrase.

An existing vault is fetched to this device first; a new vault is filled from this device's files. To use another vault, choose Sign in again or change vault. Disconnect forgets the connection on this device only; the device stays listed on the server until it is removed there.

Device credentials last 30 days and renew themselves while the device is used.
tabularium.help.connect.title: Connecting and changing vaults
tabularium.help.errors.body:
Credentials no longer valid: the device was removed on the server or its credentials expired. Sign in again.

Encryption settings refused: this device's settings differ from the vault's. Disconnect and connect again.

A rebuild is in progress: wait until the owner ends it on the web.

A note does not synchronise: check the size limit and the excluded files under Sync, and look in the log.

The first synchronisation of a large vault takes a while; keep Obsidian open until the status shows Up to date.
tabularium.help.errors.title: Common problems
tabularium.help.migrate.body:
Turn off the plug-in "self-hosted-livesync" in this vault before connecting Tabularium; the two must not run together. Then connect to the vault that already holds your notes on the Tabularium server, so this device fetches it.

The old plug-in's settings and local database are not used.
tabularium.help.migrate.title: Moving from the old plug-in
tabularium.help.passphrase.body:
Notes are encrypted on each device with the vault's passphrase before they are sent; the server cannot read them. Every device of a vault uses the same passphrase.

The passphrase cannot be recovered. If it is lost, the notes on the server cannot be decrypted; devices that still have the files can create a new vault from them.
tabularium.help.passphrase.title: The vault passphrase
tabularium.help.rebuild.body:
A rebuild replaces the vault on the server with one device's files, for example to clean up old data. The owner authorises the device on the web (Account settings, Vaults and devices, Rebuild vault), then runs Overwrite the server with this device in Maintenance on that device.

Afterwards the vault is locked. Each other device shows Vault locked and must fetch from the server. When all of them have fetched, unlock the vault here or on the web.
tabularium.help.rebuild.title: Rebuilding and unlocking
tabularium.help.status.body:
The status bar shows the connection and counters. Up to date means nothing is waiting. Changes waiting counts files that have not been sent yet; they are sent with the next synchronisation.

When the device is offline, changes are kept and sent once it is back online. A failed synchronisation is explained in the log (Maintenance, Log).
